classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate four logarithmic curves using two axis reflections and interpret the left-domain limiting behaviour.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Use reflections in the $x$- and $y$-axes to sketch the four graphs below on one set of axes.

$$y=\log_2 x,\qquad y=-\log_2 x,\qquad y=\log_2(-x),\qquad y=-\log_2(-x)$$

answer.short:
The four curves have vertical asymptote $x=0$. The two right-hand curves cross at $(1,0)$; the two left-hand curves cross at $(-1,0)$.

Reflect $y=\log_2 x$ in the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis and both axes to obtain the other three curves.
answer.worked:
Sketch $y=\log_2 x$ through $(\tfrac12,-1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,1)$, with vertical asymptote $x=0$.

Reflection in the $x$-axis gives $y=-\log_2 x$, through $(\tfrac12,1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,-1)$.

Reflection of the original curve in the $y$-axis gives $y=\log_2(-x)$, through $(-\tfrac12,-1)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(-2,1)$.

Reflection in both axes gives $y=-\log_2(-x)$, through $(-\tfrac12,1)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(-2,-1)$. Label all four curves on the same axes.

spec.description: Four equation-driven logarithmic curves on shared axes. Line styles and an external legend identify the curves without crowding the asymptote.
spec.mathematics: Axis reflections of y=log_2(x); right-domain curves intersect at (1,0), left-domain curves at (-1,0), and all have vertical asymptote x=0.
